machine.notes: An Origin 3800 of two compute racks, 001 and 002, and 64 processors: 16 four-processor C-bricks, eight in each rack, four on ports 2 to 5 of each of four eight-port R-bricks, two R-bricks to a rack. The R-bricks of a rack are joined port 1 to port 1 and 6 to 6, and the racks by four cables as the cabling draft's 64-processor table has them: port 7 to port 7 between the racks' unit-19 R-bricks and between their unit-27 R-bricks, and port 8 to the other rack's other R-brick's port 8. The draft is preliminary, so the port numbers are inferred, not established; the cable and R-brick counts match the shipped drawing, and the wiring is established as the draft's content. Each rack repeats the one-rack layout: C-bricks at bays 10, 13, 16 and 21 on the unit-19 R-brick and 24, 29, 32 and 35 on the unit-27 R-brick, so a bay repeats across the two racks and only the rack tells the bricks apart. An I-brick sits in I/O rack 101 at bay 20, the middle I/O position of the shipped rack layouts (inferred: the position is read from those layouts, not from a cabling rule). The rack name 101 for a 64-processor system's I/O rack is inferred from the numbering rule, and which C-brick the I-brick's cable reaches is unknown (the guide's I/O chapter is empty): the I-brick is cabled to the first C-brick's XIO (II) connector at its XBridge port A, a model choice and an approximation. Each R-brick presents all eight ports. The rack L2 controllers are not modelled, nor is the R-brick's USB hub traffic to the C-brick L1s. Each C-brick carries four 400 MHz R12000s with 8 MB secondary caches and, by default, 1024 MB in two 512 MB banks, the fit that keeps the stock PROM's memory test short; 4096 MB in eight 512 MB banks is accepted too. The bundles ship C-bricks without memory, so the memory is a model choice. The routers answer the model's synthetic diagnostics, which no hardware record settles. No automated check boots the stock PROM on this topology; a boot is a manual run.

variants.notes: QEMU's currently shipping 500 MHz/2 MiB Origin 300 configuration writes this exact Config0 low-25-bit reset word (readback 0x6c9aa985). No product here yet reads this field; it moves machine.firmware_config.processor_reset_mode here for a future compiler once a Bedrock-node compile path exists. The complete Config0 write mask remains unestablished for R14000, so only the literal word is carried, not a named-field encoding.

The 500 MHz C-brick PIMM. Established: SGI's C-brick owner's guide lists it with 8 MB per processor, which with the data sheet establishes the 8 MiB flash word 0x549ca985 as the stock IP35 PROM's row; the controller release notes name parts 030-1520-002 and 030-1799-001; and a public Origin 3400 inventory prints 24 such processors at revision 1.4 beside 8 MB caches. PRId 0x0f14 is established for the part revision (Linux prints PrId 0x00000f14 on Origin-class machines and IP35 hinv prints 1.4) but has not been read raw on a C-brick. Revision follows the part, not the clock: 500 MHz Origin 300 and Fuel listings print 2.4 and 2.3. Inferred: the 250 MHz cache clock and Tap 0xa, which the same revision and clock print on Onyx2 boards; the FPU identification, left at the R14000 type's 0x00000900 because no FIR has been read on an IP35 and the printed FPU 1.4 is the kernel's copy of PRId; and the Config0 mode word 0x009ca985 (read at reset as 0x6c9ca985): the low 25 bits of the flash word, fields EC 4 (200 MHz Hub), SC 3, SS 4 (8 MiB), SB 1, BE 1 and K0 5, bit 23 unknown, K0 rewritable by software (not traced). The PROM writes the flash word to Config0 and checks only that the low 16 bits (0xa985) read back. Approximated: the reset-mode word as the model's choice, the Hub clock and the FPU revision printed. Unknown: the PIMM's board lines.

The 600 MHz C-brick PIMM, part 030-1734-00x. Established by capture: a retained record of three C-bricks with six 030-1734-001 and -002 PIMMs prints Scache 8 MB, 300 MHz, Tap 0xa on all 12 processors, at revisions 2.4 (ten) and 2.3 (two). The C-brick board-identification word selecting the PROM's 600 MHz, 8 MiB row (flash word 0x549cab85) is inferred. PRId 0x0f24 is established for the part revision (Linux prints PrId 0x00000f24 on Origin-class machines and IP35 hinv prints 2.4) but has not been read raw on a C-brick; the model uses 2.4, and 2.3 (0x0f23) is inferred.
